common.navigationHelp: The panel’s navigation, as a drawer on a small screen.
common.name: Name
common.noMatchesHelp: Try a shorter search, or clear the filter.

auth.twoFactorPrompt: Enter the six-digit code from your authenticator app.
auth.signInSubtitle: Your apps, on servers you own.
auth.forgotPasswordHelp: There is no email reset on a self-hosted panel. Recover access from the server: see the troubleshooting guide.
auth.setupSubtitle: Create the first account. This takes a minute.
auth.setupTokenHelp: The installer printed this. It was also saved to /etc/skifity/setup-token on the server.
auth.teamNameHelp: You can rename this later. Projects and servers belong to a team.
auth.recoveryKeyIntro: This key can decrypt every secret {{product}} stores. Without it, a restored backup is unreadable.
auth.recoveryKeyWarning: It is shown once. Store it somewhere safe and offline, not in this panel.
auth.recoveryKeyConfirm: I have saved it somewhere safe
auth.recoveryKeyReminder: You have not saved your recovery key yet.
auth.twoFactorIntro: Scan this with an authenticator app, then enter the code it shows.
auth.recoveryCodesIntro: Each code signs you in once if you lose your phone. They are shown now and never again.
auth.recoveryCodesNone: No recovery codes left. Turn two-factor off and on again to get a new set.
auth.recoveryCodesReplaced: The codes you had before stop working.
auth.apiTokensHelp: Tokens let the CLI and AI assistants act as you. Give each one a name so you can tell them apart.
auth.tokenShownOnce: This is the only time the token is shown. Copy it now.
auth.subtitle: Your sign-in, the devices you are signed in on, and the tokens that act as you.
auth.twoFactorOff: Off. A password on its own is the only thing between anyone and this cluster.

ssoError.refused: That sign-in was refused. Try again, or sign in with a password.
ssoError.no_account: You do not have an account on this panel. Ask an administrator to invite you.
ssoError.state: That sign-in did not come back the way it left. Start again.
ssoError.expired: That sign-in took too long. Start again.
ssoError.disabled: That account has been disabled on this panel.

dashboard.title: Overview
dashboard.noServersHelp: Add your first server and {{product}} will turn it into a cluster. All you need is an IP address and a password.
dashboard.noAppsHelp: Deploy from a Git repository, a container image, or start from a template.
dashboard.clusterUnreachableHelp: Your apps keep running. {{product}} cannot make changes until it can reach the cluster again.
dashboard.notHighlyAvailableHelp: With three control plane servers, the cluster keeps working when one of them fails.

activity.subtitle: What changed in this team, newest first.
activity.emptyHelp: Everything people do in this team shows up here as it happens.

projects.title: Projects
projects.subtitle: Every app and database lives in a project, in one of its environments.
projects.emptyHelp: A project groups the apps and databases that belong together.
projects.sharedVariablesHelp: Every app in this project gets these. An app can override one with its own.
projects.canvasHelp: How this project's apps and databases connect.
projects.deleteProjectWarning: This removes every app, database and volume in it. This cannot be undone.
projects.quotaHelp: How much of what this environment is allowed has been used. A deployment that would go over is refused.
projects.quotaFull: This environment has reached a limit. New instances will not start until something is freed or the limit is raised.

schedule.label: Schedule
schedule.everyMonth: On the 1st of each month at 03:00 UTC
schedule.customHelp: Five cron fields in UTC: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.

apps.title: Apps
apps.newAppSubtitle: Deploy from a Git repository, or run a container image you already have.
apps.rootDirectoryHelp: For a monorepo: the folder this app lives in.
apps.portHelp: The port your app listens on. Most frameworks read it from the PORT variable, which {{product}} sets for you.
apps.healthPathHelp: A path that returns 200 once the app is ready to serve, such as /healthz.
apps.startCommandHelp: Leave empty to use the image’s own start command.
apps.previewEnvironmentsHelp: Each pull request gets its own copy with its own URL, removed when the pull request closes.
apps.emptyHelp: Deploy from Git, run a container image, or start from a template.
apps.logsPreviousHelp: The container that ran before this one. When an app keeps restarting, this is where it said why.
apps.logsPreviousNone: This app has not restarted, so there is no earlier log to read.
apps.restartConfirm: Restart every instance? Traffic keeps flowing: instances are replaced one at a time.
apps.deleteAppWarning: This stops the app and removes it. Volumes are kept, so their data survives.
apps.noInstancesHelp: A deployment builds the app and starts the first one.
apps.noOutputYetHelp: What a command prints appears here.
apps.runCommandHelp: Runs once, in this app's image, with this app's variables. A migration, a backfill, a look at the data.
apps.runningHelp: The command is running. Its output appears here when it finishes.
apps.runNoOutput: The command finished and printed nothing.
apps.releaseCommandHelp: Runs on every deployment, after the build and before any traffic reaches the new version. This is where a migration belongs: if it fails the deployment stops and the version that was serving keeps serving.
apps.scheduledCommandsHelp: A nightly report, an hourly cleanup. Each runs on its own, in this app's image, on the schedule you give it.
apps.scheduleHelp: Five cron fields, in UTC. "0 3 * * *" is every day at 03:00.
apps.detectedMaybe: This might be {{what}}. Nothing was filled in — check the fields below.
apps.detectedPartly: The repository is large, so only the top of it was read.
apps.composeFound: This Compose file has {{count}} service. Pick the one this app is:
apps.composeFound_other: This Compose file has {{count}} services. Pick the one this app is:
apps.composeRest: Create the other services the same way, in this environment. They reach each other by name, which is what the links in a Compose file become.

deploy.title: Deployments
deploy.rebuildHelp: Ignores the cache and builds again even if nothing changed.
deploy.imageCollectedHelp: Only the last few versions keep their image, so the disk does not fill. Deploy this commit again to get it back.
deploy.rollbackHelp: Puts back this version's image and the settings it ran with.
deploy.noDeploymentsHelp: The first deployment builds your app and gives it a URL.
deploy.reusedImage: Nothing needed building: this version was already built, so the existing image was reused.
deploy.noRebuildNeeded: Saved and rolled out. No rebuild was needed.

variables.title: Variables
variables.help: These become environment variables inside your app.
variables.secretHelp: Stored encrypted and never shown again. Use this for passwords, tokens and keys.
variables.buildTimeHelp: Values baked into the image, such as a public API URL for a front-end build. Changing one rebuilds the app.
variables.bulkEditHelp: One KEY=value per line. Paste a .env file here.
variables.invalidKey: A name can only contain letters, digits and underscores, and cannot start with a digit.
variables.rebuildQueued: Saved. This value is baked into the image, so the app is being rebuilt.

domains.title: Domains
domains.automaticHelp: {{product}} gives every app a working URL straight away, with HTTPS.
domains.dnsRecord: Create an A record for {{hostname}} pointing to {{ip}}.
domains.certificateFailed: The certificate could not be issued
domains.certificateFailedHelp: Check that the domain's DNS record points at this cluster, then remove the domain and add it again.
domains.cannotRemoveAutomatic: The automatic domain cannot be removed. It keeps the app reachable while you set up your own.

scaling.title: Scaling
scaling.automaticHelp: Skifity adds and removes instances between the numbers below, by how busy the app is.
scaling.scaleToZero: Stop when nobody is using it
scaling.scaleToZeroHelp: The app stops after a few idle minutes and starts again on the first request. The first request after that takes a few seconds.
scaling.scaleToZeroUsesRequests: While this is on, the app is scaled by how many requests are waiting rather than by CPU or memory. The most instances still applies.
scaling.readinessOk: This app looks ready to run several instances.
scaling.resourcesHelp: Reserved is what each instance is guaranteed. The limit is the most it may use before it is restarted.
scaling.spreadHelp: Instances are placed on different servers where possible, so losing one server does not take the app down.

servers.title: Servers
servers.subtitle: The machines your apps run on. Skifity joins them into one cluster.
servers.addServerIntro: Enter the address and how to sign in. {{product}} does the rest.
servers.authKeyPlaceholder: Paste the contents of your private key file
servers.passwordNotStored: Your password is used once, to install a key {{product}} owns, and is never stored.
servers.serverNameHelp: Something you will recognise, such as "Frankfurt 1".
servers.locationHelp: A label, so you can place apps near your users.
servers.controlPlaneHelp: Control plane servers run the cluster itself. Three of them keep it working when one fails.
servers.emptyHelp: Any VPS with Ubuntu or Debian works. One server is enough to start.
servers.requirementsList: Ubuntu 24.04 or Debian 12, at least 1 GB of memory, 8 GB of free disk, and SSH access as root.
servers.promote: Make it a control plane server
servers.promoteHelp: With three control plane servers, the cluster survives losing one. This moves the apps off this server first.
servers.removeServerWarning: Instances running here move to your other servers first. Nothing is lost.
servers.wipeServer: Also remove Kubernetes from the machine
servers.adopted: Skifity did not install this server
servers.adoptedHelp: It was already a node of the cluster when Skifity was installed — usually the machine the panel itself runs on. It is shown here so you can see what the cluster has, and it cannot be removed or promoted from the panel, because there is no key to it. Run the uninstaller on the machine itself to take it out.

databases.title: Databases
databases.subtitle: Managed databases, backed up and connected to your apps.
databases.storageHelp: How much disk the database gets. This can be increased later, but not reduced.
databases.emptyHelp: A managed database is backed up, restored and connected to your apps for you.
databases.credentialsWarning: Anyone with these can read and change everything in the database.
databases.linkAppHelp: The connection string is added to the app as a variable, and the app is restarted so it picks it up.
databases.backupScheduleFieldHelp: When the backup runs. Times are UTC.
databases.retentionHelp: Older backups are deleted when a new one succeeds.
databases.backupScheduleHelp: Backups are written to the storage you configured in Settings.
databases.restoreWarning: This replaces everything currently in the database with the contents of this backup. It cannot be undone.
databases.restoreStarted: Restore started. The database is unavailable until it finishes.
databases.deleteWarning: Every table, row and backup schedule goes with it. Existing backups in your storage are kept, but the panel will no longer know about them.
databases.backupStarted: The backup has started. It will appear in the list when it finishes.

templates.title: Templates
templates.subtitle: Applications that install in one step, with their databases and settings already connected.
templates.installedNote: Installed. It may take a minute to start.
templates.installedApps_one: Installed {{count}} app. It may take a minute to start.
templates.installedApps_other: Installed {{count}} apps. They may take a minute to start.

settings.title: Settings
settings.roleHelp: Owners can do anything, including removing the team. Admins manage servers and settings. Members deploy apps.
settings.secretStored: Stored. Enter a new value to replace it.
settings.componentsHelp: Heavy features are installed only when you first use them, so a fresh install stays small.
settings.rotateKeyHelp: Creates a new master key and re-encrypts every stored secret with it. Your secrets are not decrypted in the process.
settings.auditLogHelp: Who did what, when, and from where.
settings.noUpdateCheck: {{product}} does not contact any server to check for updates.
settings.rotateKeyDone: The master key was rotated and every stored secret was re-encrypted with it.
settings.rotateKeyPartial: The new master key is in place, but some secrets could not be re-encrypted. The old key was kept so they stay readable.
settings.subtitle: Everything an operator configures, in one place. Nothing here needs a file on the server.
settings.inviteLinkHelp: It is shown once, works for seven days, and can only be used once. Skifity does not send email unless you have configured SMTP.
settings.inviteMemberHelp: Invite somebody by email. Skifity gives you a link to send them; they choose their own password. Somebody who already has an account here is added directly instead.
settings.exportHelp: Everything this team has — projects, apps, domains, databases, variables and schedules — as one JSON file, with each app's Kubernetes objects beside it.
settings.exportSecrets: The value of anything marked secret is not included. Those values are already in your own cluster, as ordinary Kubernetes Secrets you have access to.
settings.pluginStoreCheckHelp: Reads the catalogue with the values as they are saved, so a wrong address or a wrong key turns up here rather than on the day you wanted a plugin.
settings.pluginStoreVerified: Signed by the key set here
settings.pluginStoreGoToPlugins: Go to Plugins to install one

cluster_flannel_backend.label: How servers talk to each other
cluster_flannel_backend.help: WireGuard encrypts traffic between your servers, which matters when they are with different providers. It needs the wireguard kernel module on every server. vxlan works everywhere and is not encrypted. Every server in a cluster has to use the same one, so change this before adding servers, not after.

cluster_k3s_version.label: Kubernetes version
cluster_k3s_version.help: The k3s version a server added from here is installed with. Leave empty to follow the stable channel, which is what a new cluster gets. Pin it to keep a server you add next month on the same version as the ones you have.

cluster_preview_ttl_days.label: Remove preview environments after
cluster_preview_ttl_days.help: Days with no deployment before a pull request's preview environment is removed. A preview that is still being pushed to survives however long the pull request stays open. Set to 0 to keep them until their pull request closes, which is how previews are normally removed — but a webhook that never arrives then leaves one running forever.

dns_api_token.label: DNS API token
dns_api_token.help: A token scoped to edit records in one zone. Do not use a global account key.

dns_provider.label: DNS provider
dns_provider.help: Lets Skifity create DNS records for you when you add a domain. Leave empty to create them yourself.

dns_zone.label: DNS zone
dns_zone.help: The zone records are created in.

domains_acme_email.label: Let's Encrypt email
domains_acme_email.help: Where Let's Encrypt sends certificate expiry warnings. Required before HTTPS certificates can be issued.

domains_acme_server.label: ACME directory URL
domains_acme_server.help: Leave empty for Let's Encrypt production. Point it at the staging directory while you are testing, so you do not hit the rate limit.

domains_cloudflare_tunnel_token.label: Cloudflare tunnel token
domains_cloudflare_tunnel_token.help: Lets your apps answer on the internet without a public IP, a port open, or a fixed address for DNS to point at. Create a tunnel in the Cloudflare dashboard under Zero Trust, Networks, Tunnels; choose the Cloudflared connector and copy the token it shows. Then add one public hostname on that tunnel — a wildcard such as *.apps.example.com covers every app at once — with the service set to HTTP and the address traefik.kube-system.svc.cluster.local:80. Install Cloudflare tunnel under Components once the token is saved.

domains_cluster_ip.label: Cluster public IP
domains_cluster_ip.help: The address your domains should point at. Detected automatically; override it if your cluster sits behind a load balancer.

domains_geo_asn_url.label: Network database
domains_geo_asn_url.help: The same, for the network a visitor's address belongs to, which is what an AS number rule tests.

domains_geo_country_url.label: Country database
domains_geo_country_url.help: Where the firewall's country data comes from, in MaxMind's .mmdb format. Leave empty for DB-IP's free monthly file, which needs no account. A %s in the address is replaced with the month. Point it at your own copy, or at a MaxMind download, if you would rather.

domains_geo_enabled.label: Look up a visitor's country and network
domains_geo_enabled.help: On by default. The firewall downloads DB-IP's free monthly databases, which need no account, so that a rule can name a country or a network. Turn it off on a cluster with no way out to the internet, or if you would rather nothing was downloaded — a rule about a country cannot then be saved, which is better than one that is quietly skipped.

domains_trusted_proxies.label: Trusted proxies
domains_trusted_proxies.help: Address ranges in front of this cluster that may say who a visitor is. The pod and service networks are trusted already; add a load balancer's range here if you have one. Get this wrong in the other direction and a visitor can choose the address your firewall rules judge them by, so add only ranges you control.

domains_wildcard.label: Wildcard domain
domains_wildcard.help: A domain with a wildcard DNS record pointing at this cluster. Every app gets a free subdomain under it. Leave empty to use sslip.io addresses instead.

email_smtp_from.label: Send email from
email_smtp_from.help: The address notifications appear to come from. It usually has to be one your mail server is allowed to send as, or the mail is rejected.

email_smtp_host.label: SMTP host
email_smtp_host.help: Needed for email notifications and for password reset emails.

email_smtp_password.label: SMTP password
email_smtp_password.help: Stored encrypted. Most providers want an app password here rather than your account password.

email_smtp_port.label: SMTP port
email_smtp_port.help: 587 for STARTTLS, which is what almost everything uses now. 465 is implicit TLS; 25 is unencrypted and usually blocked by hosting providers.

email_smtp_tls.label: Use STARTTLS
email_smtp_tls.help: Leave on unless your mail server only accepts plain connections.

email_smtp_user.label: SMTP username
email_smtp_user.help: Leave empty if your mail server accepts mail from this cluster without signing in.

general_default_builder.label: Default builder
general_default_builder.help: Which builder to use when a repository has no Dockerfile. Railpack produces smaller images; Nixpacks is older and more widely tested.

general_panel_url.label: Panel URL
general_panel_url.help: The address people use to reach this panel. Used in links inside notifications and in webhook URLs.

general_telemetry_disabled.label: Disable usage reporting
general_telemetry_disabled.help: Skifity sends nothing anywhere by default. This setting exists so that the absence of telemetry is visible rather than assumed.

maintenance_audit_history_days.label: Keep the activity log for
maintenance_audit_history_days.help: Days. The activity log is kept far longer than anything else here, because a log that forgets is most of the way to not having one. Shorten it only if you have a reason to.

maintenance_deployment_history.label: Deployment records to keep, per app
maintenance_deployment_history.help: How many past deployments an app keeps, with their build logs. Older ones are removed so the panel's database does not grow without end. Only the ten most recent can be rolled back to, because that is how many images the registry keeps and how many revisions Kubernetes itself remembers.

plugins_store_public_key.label: Plugin store signing key
plugins_store_public_key.help: The store's Ed25519 public key, base64. With one set, an index that is not signed by it is refused. With none, the catalogue is still readable and every entry is shown as vouched for by nobody. Generate a pair with: skifity admin plugin-key

plugins_store_url.label: Plugin store
plugins_store_url.help: Where the panel looks for plugins. Leave empty for the Skifity store. Point it at your own index to run a store of your own, or clear the public key below to browse one that is not signed — a plugin can always be installed from a manifest address or by pasting one, which is what a cluster with no way out to the internet uses.

registry_password.label: Registry password
registry_password.help: A token with permission to push. Stored encrypted and never shown again.

registry_url.label: External registry
registry_url.help: Where built images are pushed. Leave empty to use the registry inside the cluster, which is the simplest option.

registry_username.label: Registry username
registry_username.help: Needed only for an external registry. The registry inside the cluster needs no credentials.

signin_oidc_allowed_domains.label: Allowed email domains
signin_oidc_allowed_domains.help: Comma-separated. Only people whose verified email is in one of these domains may sign in. Leave empty to accept anybody the provider vouches for, which is only safe when the provider is yours.

signin_oidc_auto_create.label: Create an account on first sign-in
signin_oidc_auto_create.help: With this off, somebody the provider knows and this panel does not is refused, so accounts are created by invitation rather than by anyone with a company address.

signin_oidc_button_label.label: Sign-in button text
signin_oidc_button_label.help: What the button on the sign-in page says. Leave empty for a generic label.

signin_oidc_client_id.label: Client ID
signin_oidc_client_id.help: From the application you registered with the provider. Its redirect URI is this panel's address followed by /api/auth/sso/callback.

signin_oidc_client_secret.label: Client secret
signin_oidc_client_secret.help: Stored encrypted and never shown again.

signin_oidc_issuer.label: Single sign-on issuer
signin_oidc_issuer.help: The OpenID Connect issuer URL of your identity provider — Okta, Entra, Authentik, Keycloak, Zitadel, Google. Skifity reads its configuration from /.well-known/openid-configuration under this address. Leave empty to sign in with a password only.

storage_s3_access_key.label: S3 access key
storage_s3_access_key.help: Use a key that can only write to this bucket.

storage_s3_bucket.label: S3 bucket
storage_s3_bucket.help: The bucket backups are written to. Skifity does not create it for you.

storage_s3_endpoint.label: S3 endpoint
storage_s3_endpoint.help: Any S3-compatible service works: AWS, Backblaze B2, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, or a MinIO server you run yourself.

storage_s3_path_style.label: Use path-style URLs
storage_s3_path_style.help: Turn this on for MinIO and most self-hosted S3 services.

storage_s3_region.label: S3 region
storage_s3_region.help: Some providers ignore this; AWS does not.

storage_s3_secret_key.label: S3 secret key
storage_s3_secret_key.help: Stored encrypted and never shown again.

errors.copiedForAI: Copied. Paste it into your AI assistant.
errors.crashHelp: Something in the panel could not be drawn. Your apps and servers are not affected — only this screen is. Try again, or go somewhere else in the panel.
errors.pageNotFoundHelp: The link may be old, or the thing it pointed at may have been deleted.
errors.offlineHelp: Your apps keep running. This page will reconnect on its own.

git.title: Git
git.help: Connect an account so Skifity can read your private repositories and deploy when you push. A public repository needs none of this.
git.sourceNameHelp: Something you will recognise, such as "Work GitHub".
git.tokenHelp: Needs permission to read the repository and to create a webhook. Stored encrypted and never shown again.
git.baseURLHelp: For a self-hosted GitLab or Gitea. Leave empty for the hosted service.
git.disconnectWarning: Apps deployed from this account stop deploying on push. They keep running.
git.webhookURLHelp: Skifity adds this to your repositories by itself when the token allows it. If it could not, add it by hand in the repository's webhook settings.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.help: Where to tell you when something happens. Nothing is sent until you add somewhere.
notifications.eventsHelp: Choose as few as you can live with. A channel nobody reads is worse than none.
notifications.testSent: Sent. If nothing arrives, the details are wrong.

event.certificate.failed: A certificate could not be issued

invite.title: Join {{team}}
invite.subtitle: You have been invited as {{email}}, as a {{role}}. Choose a password and you are in.
invite.emailFixed: This is the address the invitation was for, and it cannot be changed here.
invite.notValidHelp: The link has expired, has been used already, or was withdrawn. Ask whoever invited you for a new one.

environments.confinementRestrictedHelp: Pods here are held to the strictest profile. An image that starts as root is refused, which is most off-the-shelf images.
environments.confinementBaselineHelp: This environment accepts an image that starts as root. A privileged container, host networking and host paths are still refused, so an app still cannot reach the server it runs on.
environments.confinementLowerTitle: Accept images that start as root?
environments.confinementLowerConfirm: Apps in this environment will be allowed to start as root inside their own container, which is what the official WordPress, Nextcloud and MediaWiki images do. A privileged container, host networking, host paths and extra capabilities stay refused. Redeploy each app for the change to reach it.

firewall.title: Firewall
firewall.help: Rules on who may reach this app: by address, by country, by network, by path or by header, combined with and and or. The first rule that matches decides.
firewall.notInstalled: These rules are not being enforced
firewall.notInstalledHelp: The firewall component is not installed, so nothing is checking requests. Install it under Settings, then Components.
firewall.noDomain: This app has no address to guard
firewall.noDomainHelp: Rules apply to a hostname. Add a domain under Domains, and these rules will start applying to it.
firewall.noGeo: A rule names a country or a network, and this panel does not look them up
firewall.noGeoHelp: Turn on "Look up a visitor's country and network" under Settings, then Domains and HTTPS. Until then, a rule like this is skipped on every request.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.subtitle: Features other people wrote, running beside the panel in a container of their own.
plugins.emptyHelp: Browse the store, or install one from an address or a manifest you paste.
plugins.removeConfirm: Its container, its settings and its access token all go. Anything it wrote elsewhere stays where it is.
plugins.secretStored: Stored. Enter a new value to replace it.
plugins.storeVerified: Signed by the key this panel trusts · {{url}}
plugins.storeUnsigned: Nobody has vouched for this catalogue
plugins.storeUnsignedHelp: No signing key is set, so the panel cannot tell whether this list is the one the store published. Set one under Settings, then Plugins. Either way, what a plugin may do is shown before you install it.
plugins.storeEmpty: The store has nothing in it
plugins.storeEmptyHelp: The catalogue was read and lists no plugins.
plugins.fromAddressHelp: A plugin can always be installed without a store — from the address of its manifest, or by pasting the manifest itself. This is the path a cluster with no way out to the internet uses, and the one a plugin author uses to try their own.
plugins.willBeAbleTo: This plugin will be able to:
plugins.noPermissions: It is not asking for access to anything.
plugins.blocksDeploys: This plugin can stop a deployment
plugins.blocksDeploysHelp: It asked to be consulted before every deploy and may refuse one. A plugin that is down does not block anything, and you can switch it off at any time.
plugins.confinementNote: It runs in a namespace of its own and can reach the panel, DNS and the internet — not your apps, not your databases, and not the server it runs on.
plugins.digestNote: Pinned by digest, so the image cannot be changed under you after you have agreed to it.
